description:
Welcome to Health Orbit! 

We are building an AI powered space health copilot to monitor and protect astronauts on deep space missions. We are actively seeking passionate minds in software development, data science, predictive AI, space biology, medicine, and UI UX design. Join us to redefine space health together!
summary: Health Orbit is onboard health monitoring software for astronauts on long-duration deep space missions. It gathers cardiovascular, sleep, radiation, exercise, behavioral and cabin environment indicators, compares every reading with the astronaut's own baseline, and turns the result into a clear status and one specific next step. Because it runs entirely on the spacecraft, it keeps working when the signal delay to Earth is measured in minutes. This answers the core of the challenge: on a mission to Mars, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for spotting changes in themselves, and Health Orbit gives them what they need to evaluate their health and act on it without waiting for ground support.
details:
How it works

1. Collect: readings from wearables, dosimeters, exercise devices and short self-reports.

2. Baseline: a personal mean and spread built from each astronaut's first 14 days of data.

3. Detect: every value is measured as a number of standard deviations from that person's baseline, and the engine checks whether a change persists across consecutive days. A single unusual reading does not raise an alert.

4. Score: each domain is rated, and the overall index is capped close to the lowest domain so one problem is never hidden by good results elsewhere.

5. Guide: every alert shows the measured value, the baseline, the size of the change, how long it has lasted, and a concrete action.

Prototype

The prototype runs on simulated data for a four-person crew on day 142 of a Mars transit. The Commander is nominal, the Pilot shows developing fatigue, the Flight Engineer shows a decline in wellbeing consistent with isolation, and the Mission Specialist's exercise has fallen well below prescription. Users can run a solar particle event drill that triggers a crew-wide shelter warning, take a working reaction time test, submit a daily check-in and log exercise, and every score updates immediately. A landing page introduces the project and lets visitors switch between Earth, the Moon and Mars.

Benefits and intended impact

- Catches early changes that fixed population thresholds miss, because each astronaut is compared with their own normal.

- Explains every alert, so the crew can see why the system is concerned and trust its output.

- Works without a connection to Earth and stores the full record for the flight surgeon to review later.

- Supports crew autonomy on missions where real-time medical support is not possible.

Tools and technologies

HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks or server. Charts and planet visuals are drawn with the HTML Canvas API, and planet textures are generated in a Web Worker. It runs in any modern browser on desktop, tablet or phone.

What makes it creative

Instead of fixed thresholds, Health Orbit judges each astronaut against their own baseline and explains its reasoning in plain language, so the crew can act on it with confidence while minutes away from help.
